title: The Daily Average of Homicides in Chiapas Has Fallen 64% Since the Start of the Current Administration
author: Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz,%20enviada)
originally appeared in the [September 11, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/11/politica/se-han-
reducido-64-el-promedio-diario-de-homicidios-en-chiapas-desde-el-inicio-del-
actual-gobierno-snsp), Mexico’s premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas**. In the nearly two years of the current federal
administration, there has been a **64 percent drop in the daily average of
homicides** in the state, reported Marcela Figueroa, head of the Executive
Secretariat of the National Public Security System. At the VII Military
Region, where the morning press conference was held, she explained that high-
impact crimes also fell **43 percent** , above all extortion, kidnappings, and
femicides. Vehicle theft dropped 68 percent.

Omar García Harfuch, Secretary of Security and Citizen Protection, said that
from October 1 to August 31, **9,949 people were arrested** , and 1,544
firearms and 18.7 tons of drugs were seized. He highlighted 101,907 operations
by the joint institutional force, which have enabled significant arrests such
as that of Roger Iradier “N,” alias “El Peque,” an operator of the Jalisco New
Generation Cartel in Chiapas who was on Interpol’s red notice. He noted that
from August 1 to September 11, 3.7 tons of cocaine and 2,459 liters of fuel
were seized.

Eduardo Ramírez, the state governor, for his part highlighted the work of 800
members of the Pakal rapid-reaction force, and said that with crime-prevention
programs, Tapachula and Tuxtla Gutiérrez left the top spots for insecurity
and, in the case of security, “it has come to rank around number 40.” He
stated that the prison population has grown, with nearly ten thousand people
arrested, but the level of crime has fallen.

Among other figures, he mentioned 366 state and investigative police officers,
as well as three commanders being prosecuted for criminal association.
